content: If you are allergic to this medication or have any other allergies, inform your doctor or pharmacist immediately. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could trigger allergic reactions or other complications. This medication is not recommended for use during pregnancy as it may not be effective in pregnant women. If you become pregnant or suspect you might be pregnant, notify your doctor immediately. It is currently unknown whether this medication passes into breast milk. Drug interactions can alter the effectiveness of your medications or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not list all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all products you use, including prescription, non-prescription drugs, and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This medication may slow the elimination of other drugs from your body, potentially affecting their function. Conversely, other medications may influence the elimination of cobicistat from your body, which could impact its effectiveness. Examples of such drugs include certain seizure medications (e.g., carbamazepine, phenobarbital, phenytoin, primidone), enzalutamide, specific HIV NNRTI drugs (e.g., efavirenz, etravirine, nevirapine), mitotane, and rifampin. This medication may reduce the effectiveness of hormonal birth control methods such as pills, patches, or rings, potentially leading to pregnancy. Discuss with your doctor or pharmacist whether you should use reliable backup birth control methods while taking this medication. In the event of an overdose with serious symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Laboratory and/or medical tests (e.g., kidney function) may be conducted before starting this medication and periodically while you are taking it. Ensure you attend all medical and laboratory appointments. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is less than 12 hours before your next dose, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication in its original container at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. It is not a substitute for individual medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. Take this medication by mouth with food as directed by your doctor, usually once daily. It is crucial to continue taking this medication (and other HIV medications) exactly as prescribed by your doctor. This medication works best when the drug level in your body is kept constant. Take it at evenly spaced intervals. Do not take more or less of this drug than prescribed, and do not stop taking it (or other HIV medications) without your doctor’s approval, even for a short time. Nausea may occur as a side effect. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefit to you outweighs the risk of side effects. As your immune system strengthens, it may begin to fight off infections you already had, potentially causing disease symptoms to reappear. You may also experience symptoms if your immune system becomes overactive. This reaction can occur at any time, either shortly after starting HIV treatment or many months later. A severe allergic reaction to this drug is rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice regarding side effects.
